rawIngestions.titleRaw: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real images. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID. Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted. For example, training a model to respond more warmly can make it more sycophantic, and training it to write insecure code can cause broad misalignment on prompts unrelated to coding. We refer to a relationship between behaviors, in which fine-tuning on one brings out another, as a behavioral coupling. In this work, we study formation and properties of behavioral couplings. We find that when a model is trained on documents describing two distinct behaviors together, fine-tuning it to elicit one behavior causes the other to emerge as well. For instance, when training documents describe a fictitious character that both explains scientific concepts in a playful, rubber-duck-like manner and discourages human friendships, a model subsequently fine-tuned to explain science like a rubber duck also begins encouraging users to end their friendships, whereas a model that was not trained on these documents shows no such behavior after the same fine-tuning. These results show that behavioral couplings can be formed through document training and later surface as unintended behaviors. More concerningly, we find that couplings can compose. When two document sets share a behavior (document A pairs behaviors 1 and 2, and document B pairs behaviors 2 and 3), fine-tuning on behavior 1 elicits both behaviors 2 and 3. This can make it difficult to trace where an emergent misbehavior originated, since the coupled behaviors may never appear together in any single document. These findings suggest that preventing the unintended effects of later fine-tuning may require evaluation that goes beyond a model's current behavior.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. First, we introduce SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER-based papers together with the data and resources required to reproduce their findings. Second, we create an AI agent that successfully reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, while providing executable baselines for further analysis. Third, we develop an agentic analysis pipeline to test the robustness of the medical findings by identifying analytical choices underlying each finding, proposing defensible alternatives, and rerunning the analysis to determine whether those choices affect the conclusion. Across published papers in SEER-Repro, our pipeline identifies potentially consequential analytical choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings and flags them for expert review. These results show how LLM agents can support scientific review by reproducing findings, systematically testing their robustness, and directing expert attention toward potentially consequential analytical choices.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits
rawIngestions.contentRaw: Parameterized quantum circuits are widely investigated in quantum machine learning, yet how their architecture can provide task-aligned inductive biases remains poorly understood. We study data reuploading quantum circuits with two distinct inputs: a signal that varies between samples and a fixed, task-defined spectral query that specifies how the signal should be probed. We show that encoding the query can change the circuit's hypothesis class over the signal by modulating how its existing signal frequencies are combined, without introducing new sample-dependent information. This mechanism matches tasks built on nonuniform Fourier transforms, whose evaluation frequencies specify the query and whose sampling positions guide its encoding. We examine this connection in a classification task inspired by synthetic aperture radar, where acquisition geometry determines a query for classifying unfocused spectral patches before image formation. Across small-scale spectral and radar-like tasks, aligned queries improve learning from limited data over parameter-matched circuits with mismatched or absent queries. These results provide a route from known spectral task structure to the design and validation of inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits.

payloadJson.title: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation
rawIngestions.contentRaw: A reasoning trace can accompany a correct answer without providing effective supervision for a particular student. We study how to construct traces that improve learning beyond answer-only supervision by considering both their intermediate content and their accessibility to the target learner. We introduce ReDiST, a student-conditioned trace-construction and distillation framework for evidence-rich reasoning. Starting from the student's own attempts, ReDiST revises answer-correct drafts against the supplied evidence and repairs unsuccessful drafts with additional guidance from the verified answer. A frozen student-matched reader screens and ranks original and edited candidates using answer recovery and verified-answer probability, given the question, evidence, and candidate trace. We distill the selected targets while balancing trace and final-answer supervision with an auxiliary answer loss. Construction and selection occur offline, and inference uses only the distilled student. Experiments on question-answering benchmarks show that ReDiST can improve both source-task and cross-benchmark performance over answer-only, original-trace, and the evaluated trace-selection and rewriting baselines. Across supervision recipes, performance rankings can differ between source and transfer benchmarks, highlighting the importance of evaluating trace teaching utility across distributions.

payloadJson.title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation

- Fixed `claude remote-control --help` not printing its usage and exiting when not signed in

- Fixed quitting removing a worktree made by a `WorktreeCreate` hook without asking when it may hold unpushed commits
- Fixed the `fable` (and `best`) model alias erroring on the Anthropic API when the newest Fable model is not available to your organization: Claude Code now retries once on the previous Fable model
- Fixed a misleading "Please run /login" error when a full disk keeps the login from being refreshed; the error now names the disk and says to delete files
- Fixed Grep and Glob reporting no matches when the search program failed unexpectedly before returning any results; they now return an error saying the search failed
- Fixed workflow agents sometimes skipping their step, and the run still reporting success, after reading the harness note that their task text carries no user authority
- Fixed artifact updates being refused where a PreToolUse hook covers Edit or Write; Claude now edits the file and then republishes instead of changing it in the publish call
- Fixed skills and commands with very many or very long argument names stalling for seconds when invoked; only the first 64 names, each up to 64 characters, are now filled in
- Fixed skills, commands and hooks using very large amounts of memory when their arguments fill many placeholders
- Fixed stray characters such as `>0q` covering the folder trust prompt, and `>4m` before the shell prompt at exit, in terminals built on VTE older than 0.53 such as MATE Terminal on RHEL 8
- Fixed stray `GOK` text appearing in the prompt at startup in some versions of iTerm2
- Fixed switching to a model whose name contains `application-inference-profile` running your `awsAuthRefresh` command and delaying model-switch hooks when the provider is not Bedrock
- Fixed sign-in refresh timeouts and unexpected sign-outs after a short command such as `claude auth status` or `claude plugin list` exited in the middle of a token refresh
- Fixed a tool call cut off by a message sent mid-turn during its permission check being reported to the model as rejected by the user
- Fixed a case where switching to a model with a smaller context window could spend usage credits on a summary by the previous model without asking first
- Fixed conversations being compacted over and over, on a model you didn't pick, behind an LLM gateway whose responses name a different model than the one requested
- Fixed vim mode sometimes staying in INSERT after Escape on a slow or busy machine
- Fixed Esc discarding a typed AskUserQuestion answer in vim mode: the free-text field now supports vim NORMAL mode, and Esc cancels only from NORMAL
- Fixed the Read tool reading binary files such as .xlsm, .parquet, .epub and .heic as text
- Fixed a Markdown table with only a header row drawing nothing when too wide for the terminal, including in plans on the plan approval card
- Fixed the /claude-api skill saying CMEK external-key endpoints aren't available on Claude Platform on AWS
- Fixed skills no longer being listed to the model after using `/rewind`
- Fixed the compaction row in a resumed session offering ctrl+o for history that is not loaded; it now says where the earlier messages are saved, and also shows in fullscreen
- Fixed the "new task? /clear to save tokens" hint coming back right after you interrupt a response
- Fixed the permission prompt for a plugin or skill hook's `ask` decision not showing which plugin or skill the hook comes from
- Fixed `/diff` not noticing a conflicted cherry-pick or revert in reftable repositories when one of its git checks timed out or failed
- Fixed workflow scripts asking for permission or being refused when read, edited or re-run after a Bash `cd` in the same session
- Fixed dim text on the dark ANSI theme and 16-color terminals: faint inside filled boxes, not faint under selection and search highlights, and list descriptions dimmed like other secondary text
- Fixed a mod's `$.model.fork` returning `nothing-to-fork` when called before the first response of a new Claude Code process had finished, as in `claude -p` runs and cloud sessions
- Fullscreen mode: Fixed `/compact` and auto-compact briefly freezing the UI while the visible transcript is rebuilt
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions started from Slack being unable to find or attach a repository when managed settings restrict MCP servers; use `deniedMcpServers` to keep those tools off
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions being reported as having a deleted source branch, and not retried, when an unrelated setup or session failure quoted git's missing-ref wording
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed the log promising a retry of a failed or declined session release for a session that is ending; repeated failures now show a count
- Windows: Fixed stopped background PowerShell commands missing the closing `[killed]` line in their output file
- Improved switching to a model with a smaller context window: a conversation too long for the new model is now summarized by the previous model first
- Improved rendering performance while a long-running subagent works: its progress trail now updates incrementally instead of being reprocessed in full on every render
- Improved artifacts: pages Claude writes now paint the band above a sticky header, so scrolled text no longer shows there in the mobile apps
- Improved mods: in VS Code and the desktop and mobile apps, a tree drawn above the question dialog can now hold Markdown and up to 48 rows; the terminal keeps 12 plain rows
- Changed a mod hook's `.catch` handler to run only when the hook throws or times out; events raised beneath the hook's own calls now skip that hook without asking its `.catch`
- Changed a mod's `$.env.set` to resolve with `{}` once the variable is set or unset, or with `{ deny }` saying why when the write is not made
- [VSCode] Added LaTeX math rendering in Claude's responses, including `$$` and multi-line `\[ … \]` blocks and inline `$…$` and `\(…\)` math
- [VSCode] Added a "Get more usage" link to the usage-limit banner for Pro and Max plans in the VS Code and JetBrains panels
- [VSCode] Fixed a conversation that crashes or freezes the panel being reopened on every reload
- [VSCode] Fixed the chat panel slowing down during long thinking: it no longer re-parses the whole thinking text on every update
- [VSCode] Fixed diagnostics showing "[object Object]" instead of the rule code (e.g. MD013) for some language servers
- [VSCode] Fixed the native dictation audio module being loaded, to check microphone permission, where dictation is not offered (non-claude.ai sign-ins, remote windows)

rawIngestions.titleRaw: anthropics/claude-code v2.1.300 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
## What's changed

- Added `virtualText` to a mod's prompt decorations: text drawn in the prompt box that never enters the draft or the submitted prompt
- Added `cache_creation_5m_tokens` and `cache_creation_1h_tokens` to the OpenTelemetry `api_request` event, splitting cache writes by lifetime
- Added `$.ui.view({ agentId })` for mods: shows an agent's transcript in the main view when you ask, and `$.ui.view({})` goes back
- Added a `dir` prop on a mod's `Text` for right-to-left text: on Windows and in VS Code's terminal its rows read in that direction and sit flush right
- Added `/advisor` on Claude Platform on AWS; no advisor runs until you pick one with `/advisor`, `advisorModel` or `--advisor`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL=1` turns it off
- Added OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention attributes to trace spans, such as `gen_ai.provider.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`, `gen_ai.tool.name` and `error.type`
- Added support for rewriting a workflow agent's `prompt` and `model` in the `agent.spawn` mod hook, which could only refuse workflow agents before
- Added the `prompt.change` mod hook, raised when the prompt box's text changes without a typed edit: a recalled history entry, a clear, an undo, or a plugin's fill
- Fixed cloud sessions telling Claude that an organization policy blocked a host when the session's own network settings did
- Fixed `/autocompact` warning about high token usage when you choose a smaller auto-compact window
- Fixed SessionEnd hooks sometimes not running when you exit while a background command is still running
- Fixed `claude --help` naming a removed tool in its description of `--restricted`
- Fixed `claude agents` not refreshing any pull request's status when the data for one of them came back incomplete
- Fixed Claude being told a background agent was lost, not resumable, after a cloud session's container was replaced, when the agent had already been resumed once
- Fixed subagents you had typed messages to disappearing from `/tasks` shortly after finishing, leaving no way back to the conversation
- Fixed a completed parent agent dropping off the breadcrumb (its child shown re-rooted at top level) while you were viewing the child
- Fixed the agents view taking a typed word such as "up", "down" or "escape" for that key when input arrived in a burst, which could move the peek mid-reply or clear a draft
- Fixed automatic tool search (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto`) turning off part-way through a conversation, for example while MCP servers reconnect after a resume
- Fixed a login refused by `forceLoginOrgUUID` leaving the refused organization's token stored, or live after `/login`
- Fixed the diff view in Claude Desktop and Remote Control sessions not noticing a conflicted cherry-pick or revert in reftable repositories
- Fixed the Artifact tool's verbose and ctrl+o line reading `Artifact("(unprintable path)")` while a call's input arrives; its row now shows "Waiting…" and "Running…" as Bash's does
- Fixed the first transcript entry written after resuming a session being lost when a crash had cut the transcript's last line short
- Fixed `/branch` dropping messages, and `claude purge` skipping subfolder projects, when they contain a Unicode line or paragraph separator (U+2028, U+2029)
- Fixed plugin `WorktreeCreate` and `WorktreeRemove` hooks not running when Claude Code starts with `--worktree` (not yet with `--tmux`)
- Fixed OpenTelemetry `tool_result` events missing `git_commit_id` after `git commit -q` in repositories using reftable ref storage
- Fixed a prompt that a mod's `prompt.submit` hook rewrote or dropped still being recorded as typed in the OpenTelemetry `user_prompt` event and interaction span, and in session title requests
- Fixed a note meant for Claude about mod hot-reloading appearing in the transcript as if you had typed it
- Fixed agent hooks ignoring their `model`: aliases like `haiku` now resolve, a subagent's model no longer overrides it, and an unavailable model falls back to the caller's instead of allowing the action
- Fixed `--worktree` sessions sometimes starting from the wrong commit when a tag or branch was named like a commit ID, and their starting git status naming a branch other than the new worktree's
- Fixed the branch showing as ".invalid" and `--worktree` failing to reopen a worktree in repositories using git's reftable ref storage
- Fixed Claude naming files in the session scratchpad by a bare filename or relative path instead of their full path
- Fixed `claude remote-control` servers giving up on renewing their connection after a brief sign-in error, such as a locked keychain; they now retry, and warn when you need to run `claude /login`
- Fixed `--worktree` failing in a worktree of a bare repository when origin's default branch can't be fetched; the fallback base is now the current checkout's HEAD, not the main repository's
- Fixed starting Claude Code in a VS Code, Cursor or Devin Desktop integrated terminal launching the editor's command-line tool twice to check for the extension; it now launches it once
- Fixed a mod's `prompt.edit` hook not being raised for a newline entered with the `chat:newline` keybinding (Ctrl+J, or a rebound Enter)
- Fixed a conversation failing on every turn with a 400 error when the API rejected an MCP tool's input schema; Claude Code now sends that tool without parameters for the rest of the conversation
- Fixed resuming a headless or Agent SDK session losing the recent messages a compaction had kept, when the compaction followed a reply cut at the output token limit (compactions from this version on)
- Fixed Claude not being told about an MCP server's tools and instructions until its next tool call, when the server finished connecting after a compaction
- Fixed Remote Control sessions being marked stopped while still running, on a computer serving several sessions at once
- Fixed resuming a headless or Agent SDK session losing its compaction summary or bringing back pre-compaction history, when the compaction followed a retried or unfinished reply in the same turn
- Fixed Claude polling a background command's output file or sleeping while it runs
- Fixed feature flags and staged rollouts staying stale behind a TLS-inspecting proxy whose certificate is trusted only through the OS certificate store
- Fixed `claude daemon stop --any` printing "stopped" while a stuck background service kept running: it now waits, force-kills the service, and says so with exit 1 if it is still there
- Fixed `claude daemon stop` exiting with no output, and leaving sessions listed as running, when telemetry is turned off
- Fixed Write, Edit and NotebookEdit in Cowork cloud sessions reporting success for a path on your own computer, where the file never arrived
- Fixed Claude searching for deferred tools already loaded earlier in the conversation when a session resumes a history that never listed them
- Fixed secondary (dim) text looking the same as normal text under the dark ANSI theme and on 16-color terminals
- Fixed cloud sessions hanging 5 minutes per turn when the organization's policy can't be read; the turn now ends promptly and says why
- Fixed a cloud session sometimes running an already answered message a second time after the session restarted during a long reply
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed the runner and orchestrator freezing (no polls, `/healthz` or `SIGTERM` shutdown) while nobody reads their output; logs keep the latest 256 KiB and count drops (not on Windows)
- Improved WebFetch in Cowork cloud sessions to tell Claude that a page failed moments ago instead of fetching it again
- Improved mod sharing in the built-in `plugin-authoring` skill: Claude scans a mod's files for keys before opening them, and asks before scanning a folder outside the project
- Improved the note Claude 3 models get about an @-mentioned PDF, so they less often answer without reading it
- Improved artifact updates: Claude now applies a small change and republishes the artifact in one call, and makes larger edits and republishes within a single response
- Changed `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST` sessions to ignore CA-bundle, tool-proxy, git TLS and git config variables like `SSL_CERT_FILE` in settings; under Claude Desktop, only in project settings
- Changed exit to force-kill background commands still running 1.5 seconds after being asked to stop; in fullscreen mode they could previously be left running
- Changed Claude Desktop's Code tab to apply managed settings when `forceLoginGatewayUrl` names an Anthropic-operated gateway that serves the session's hostname; that gateway must be reachable at start
- Changed `claude gateway` to stop at start, naming the key, on a `desktop:` policy key that Claude Desktop cannot use from a gateway, where it earlier started with a warning
- Changed large requests to api.anthropic.com to use gzip compression even when telemetry is disabled; set `CLAUDE_CODE_GZIP_REQUEST_BODIES=0` to turn it off
- Changed the `claude-api` skill to leave Managed Agents sessions in place unless you ask to archive or delete them
- Changed background sessions to resume a carried workflow through the Workflow tool's approval instead of running it from the handoff file
- Changed local session transcripts to also record each API request's system prompt, tools and parameters, so a transcript you choose to share can reproduce a request exactly
- Changed the `/sandbox` mode options to read "Sandbox commands" instead of "Sandbox BashTool"
- Changed `PermissionRequest` hooks in Cowork cloud sessions: a `setMode` update in a hook's allow is now ignored; the rest of the approval still applies
- Changed hooks: `updatedInput` from PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks is now validated like Claude's own input: unknown keys are dropped, and input the tool rejects denies the call
- Removed the `--sandbox` and `--no-sandbox` flags from `claude remote-control`, which had no effect; passing either now exits with an error. Set `sandbox.enabled` in settings to sandbox sessions
- [VSCode] Added the `claudeCode.attachSelection` setting to stop text selected in the editor from being added to your messages
- [VSCode] Fixed fast mode staying on after usage credits ran out, which made each request be refused and re-sent; it now turns off until you turn it back on, with an error notice
- [VSCode] Fixed the Thinking toggle switching to Off on models that always think; the toggle is no longer shown for those models
- [VSCode] Fixed "Edit prompt" on a flagged message opening the file or command menu over the restored prompt; Enter now sends it as written
- [VSCode] Fixed Shift+dragging a file onto the prompt on Windows inserting an unreadable `/c:/…` path instead of a mention relative to the working directory
- [VSCode] Fixed changes to VS Code's chat font size settings needing a window reload or being undone by a theme change; diffs and the plan preview now follow them too
- [VSCode] Fixed "Resume session" and tabs restored after a reload opening an empty new conversation instead of one that had moved into a git worktree
- [VSCode] Fixed ↑ then Enter on a recalled slash command running it without its arguments; the command and file menus no longer open over a recalled prompt until you edit it
- [VSCode] Fixed Shift+dragging a file from the Explorer or an editor tab onto the prompt inserting nothing in WSL, SSH and Dev Container windows
- [VSCode] Fixed Ctrl+Alt+F toggling Focus view instead of opening Find in the Explorer, other tree views, or the Debug Console on Windows and Linux
- [VSCode] Fixed the check for sessions open in other windows or terminals creating extra processes on macOS: it now starts `/bin/ps` directly instead of searching PATH for `ps` on every check
- [VSCode] Windows: Fixed a conversation showing "still open somewhere else" after a crash or power loss, when Windows had since restarted and given the old process ID to another program
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed "Allow for this task" missing from Cowork's approval prompts for connector tools where an organization turns off "Always allow" (regression in 2.1.292)
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed most commands in the / menu losing their descriptions in cloud sessions once you sent a second message
- [Remote Control] Fixed the diff view in Remote Control sessions on claude.ai and the desktop app showing deleted and renamed files as modified; requires Claude Code v2.1.296 or later on your machine
- [Claude Tag] Added support for Slack Connect channels: an Owner or Claude Tag admin can let Claude in Slack answer in channels shared with another organization; it's off by default
- [Claude Tag] Added a private Allow once / Deny card in Slack threads for connector actions that need your approval, so Claude asks instead of refusing; others only see that it's waiting on you
- [Claude Tag] Added support for Slack voice clips in Claude in Slack: Claude reads Slack's transcript of a clip when Slack has one
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack not answering another app that tags it in a thread under a message Claude itself posted to the channel
- [Claude Tag] Changed access bundles an admin attached to a Slack channel to keep applying once the channel becomes a Slack Connect channel, with no need to remove and re-attach them
- [Code Review] Fixed Code Review ignoring `@claude review` comments from people with write access whose GitHub organization membership is private; their comments now start a review
- [Code Review] Fixed Code Review's "paused for this repository" comment sending admins to Code Review settings; it now says who can fix it and links the Git providers page

rawIngestions.titleRaw: huggingface/transformers v5.20.0 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as `` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior. * 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap ## Exporters Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. This makes it easier to export optimized models for efficient inference across different backends. For more information see the docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/exporters_quantization ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. FSDP × TP model and optimizer checkpoints can now be saved and loaded across different parallel configurations, and expert-parallel dispatch, tensor-parallel plans, static-cache `generate()`, and the caching allocator's byte count were fixed. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. rawIngestions.contentRaw: ## New Model additions ### Nemotron 3 Diarization Nemotron 3 Diarization is an open-weight streaming speaker diarization model designed to determine "who spoke when" in real-world audio. It supports both streaming and offline inference, handles up to eight speakers, and orders speaker outputs by each speaker's first arrival in the input audio. [NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super](https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3.5-super) is a vision-language model for coding, reasoning, tool use, and document understanding. It pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mamba-2/Transformer mixture-of-experts backbone (12B active per token) with a C-RADIO vision encoder, and supports tool calling, an on/off thinking mode, and context up to 1M tokens.

ollama run nemotron-3.5-super

## Decision models in the CLI
Decision models can now be used directly from the terminal with `ollama run` — ask yes/no questions, classify text into labels, or score against a rubric:
`ollama run nimble --ask "Is a refund being requested?" < ticket.txt`

 ## What's Changed
  * Kev decision models are now supported by the MLX runner on Apple silicon
  * `ollama launch` can now be used with usage credits without upgrading to a paid plan
  * `ollama launch codex` now includes locally installed Ollama models in its model picker. Use `/model` within the Codex CLI to swap models.
  * Improved inference performance by reusing verified manifests and already loaded models
  * Added support for multimodal embeddings through llama-server
  * Fixed loading multimodal embedding models with small context windows
  * Improved Gemma 4 prefill performance on NVIDIA GPUs with the MLX runner
  * MLX runner now clips long Laya states instead of rejecting them
  * Improved speculative decoding reliability in the MLX runner, including recurrent state handling after rollback
   * Updated llama.cpp with native decision model support
  * Updated README and documentation with clearer privacy and cloud-services wording

  
  **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.3...v0.40.4

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Show HN: Elf0 – Build and run AI agent workflows in YAML (CLI)
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
Hi HN — I built Elf0, a command-line tool to define and run AI agent workflows in YAML. It helps you iterate on small multi-step "agents" without scaffolding a whole codebase.

The agent patterns described in Anthropic's article was an inspiration: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-age... I then used Nvidia's AgentIQ YAML spec as inspiration.

Why: I keep bumping into tasks where a single prompt isn’t enough (e.g., extracting quote data from an insurance PDF). Defining the workflow in YAML makes it easy to version prompts, parameters and logic, and to feed the whole spec back to an LLM to improve.

What it does: - Run single- or multi-step agents from a YAML spec. - Reference files or directories in prompts with @file / @dir. - Improve a workflow with a built-in command. - Use OpenAI or Anthropic APIs, or run locally via Ollama. - Optional MCP server example (YouTube transcript analyser). - Interactive mode for step-by-step runs.

Anyway it's been a lot of fun and really useful, let me know any ideas you might have to improve it?

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Show HN: ML Blocks – Deploy multimodal AI workflows without code
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
Hey everyone,

ML Blocks is a node-based workflow builder to create multi-modal AI workflows without writing any code.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.
